S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving a battery, including overheating whether or not it results in fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage, to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days after learning of it, and notify affected customers within 10 calendar days. A fatality or incident presenting an imminent risk to other units must be reported to the regulator within 24 hours, with an initial customer safety notice within 48 hours where a hazard may remain.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Before purchase, each prospective customer must receive the model’s numerical 55 °C failure rate directly and privately, together with clear information about material hazards, safe operating instructions, and any regulator-required precautions. Exceeding 5% is not by itself an automatic prohibition on sale or service; the regulator shall determine proportionate additional measures based on the evidence, corrective actions, and risk to users and the public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed on the effective date, manufacturers must offer a compatible retrofit or replacement pathway and complete the program within 6 years, prioritizing higher-risk units.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression suitable for the unit’s battery chemistry and installation environment. The regulator may approve an equivalent protective design where it provides comparable fire-risk reduction.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and submit the model for an independent risk review. The regulator must require a recall, including stopping sale and providing repair, replacement, or refund, when the review finds that a recall is necessary to protect users or the public; otherwise it must order proportionate corrective action and follow-up, with its decision and rationale made public.

document.section_notes: The final rules remove the automatic 5% sales ban (S2) and replace the automatic 8-per-100k recall with an independent review and regulator-discretion recall (S5), which protects both flagships from automatic market exclusion. Customers receive numerical per-model test rates privately, and publication to the general public is expressly barred. S3 (24-month new-unit deadline, 6-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month suppression) sit outside the answer-key acceptable ranges on timing, while S1 requires reporting of all thermal incidents within 5 days, with the 24-hour clock applying only to fatalities or imminent-risk incidents.
